function_v0.doc:
Stakes `amount` of `asset` (already transferred to this contract by
the caller \xe2\x80\x94 see vault-factory's fund_vault) into `pool_id` on the
vault's behalf. `pool_id` is an off-chain-computed hint (whichever
pool currently has the best yield, per blendRates.ts) \xe2\x80\x94 this contract
still executes the actual token movement on-chain, so a wrong or
malicious hint can only mean a worse pool, never a way to divert
funds, since `to`/`from`/`spender` on the Blend call are always this
contract's own address.

Only callable by the configured vault-factory (`vault_factory` here
must be the caller authorizing this invocation \xe2\x80\x94 Soroban satisfies
this automatically for a contract calling another contract with its
own address, no separate signature needed).
function_v0.name: stake

function_v0.doc:
Swaps this contract's WASM in place, keeping the same contract ID
and all existing storage (positions, admin, pool allowlist) intact \xe2\x80\x94
the standard Soroban upgrade pattern. Same rationale as
vault-factory's `upgrade`: without this, any future fix requires a
brand-new contract and orphans every vault's still-open position.
function_v0.name: upgrade

function_v0.doc:
Unstakes a vault's *full* position (principal + all accrued yield so
far) and closes it out \xe2\x80\x94 used for a `Manual` release, or a
`Schedule`/`Pct` drip's final interval, so the last payment captures
whatever yield accrued rather than leaving dust stranded with no
more scheduled withdrawals. Sends straight to `vault_factory`
(skipping an extra transfer hop through this contract).
function_v0.name: unstake_full

function_v0.doc:
One-time setup. `admin` should be a multisig, same requirement as
vault-factory's admin (FR-2.6) \xe2\x80\x94 this contract can move staked funds.

A Soroban constructor (Protocol 22+), invoked atomically by the
`CreateContractV2` host operation in the same transaction as
deployment \xe2\x80\x94 see vault-factory's `__constructor` for why a
post-deploy `initialize` function (even with `require_auth`) leaves a
race window an attacker can win by naming themselves admin first, and
why a constructor closes it structurally rather than just narrowing
it.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Reports a vault's current staked value (principal + accrued interest
so far), without unstaking anything \xe2\x80\x94 this is a read-only call, never
a real Blend withdrawal. Uses the pool's *current* `b_rate` against
this vault's tracked share count, so the number moves as Blend's
interest accrues, the same way a wallet balance would.
function_v0.name: get_vault_value

function_v0.doc:
Unstakes exactly `amount` from a vault's position, leaving the
remainder staked \xe2\x80\x94 used for `Schedule`/`Pct` drip intervals that
aren't the vault's last. The position is *not* closed: the vault
keeps earning yield on what's left.
function_v0.name: unstake_partial

function_v0.doc:
Adds or removes a Blend pool from the set this adapter may call.
Pool contracts receive token-moving authority during `submit`, so an
arbitrary off-chain rate hint must never become an arbitrary contract
invocation. The configured multisig admin owns this risk boundary.
function_v0.name: set_pool_allowed

udt_struct_v0.doc:
What a vault is currently staked into. The Blend pool is the source of
truth for the position's real *value* (principal + accrued interest) \xe2\x80\x94
`shares` never caches that value directly. It only records how many
bTokens this vault's share of the adapter's pooled Blend position
represents, measured as a balance delta around each stake/unstake call
(Blend has no concept of per-vault positions; every vault's funds sit
under this adapter's own address). Combined with the pool's current
`b_rate` (see `get_vault_value`), that's enough to report a live value
without executing a withdrawal.
udt_struct_v0.name: Position

fields.doc:
Reentrancy guard, same pattern and rationale as vault-factory's
`Vault.releasing`: stake()/unstake_full()/unstake_partial() can't
know this position's final share count until Blend's `pool.submit()`
returns, so the usual "write final state before any external call"
ordering isn't available. Set true immediately before calling into
Blend, checked at entry, cleared on the final storage write.
fields.name: processing

cases.doc: A vault may add to its existing position, but it may not silently\nswitch pool or asset while funds remain in the original position.
cases.name: PositionMismatch

cases.doc: stake()/unstake_full()/unstake_partial() reentrancy guard tripped \xe2\x80\x94\nthis position already has one of those calls in flight. See\n`Position.processing`'s doc comment.
cases.name: PositionBusy

void_v0.doc: The only address permitted to call stake/unstake (vault-factory).
void_v0.name: VaultFactory

tuple_v0.doc: Blend pools explicitly approved by the yield-adapter admin.
tuple_v0.name: AllowedPool
